draft.title: Spread of financial crises
card: A financial crisis is a sudden shock to banks and money markets. Banks fail or stop lending, and people and firms lose savings and jobs.
Banks and economies are linked. Banks lend to each other across borders, invest in each other's countries and trade goods and services.
Because of these links, trouble in one country can spread. Banks that lose money in one place cut their lending in others, and falling demand hurts countries that sell to it.
The 2008 global financial crisis began with the United States housing and banking system. It spread worldwide, and many countries saw slower growth and rising unemployment.
draft.remember: Links between banks and economies let a crisis in one country spread to others.

a.q: Why can a banking crisis in one country affect many other countries?
opts: Banks and economies are linked by lending and trade
Every country uses exactly the same banks
Crises are caused by the weather in all places
Countries must copy the laws of larger countries
a.why: Banks lend and invest across borders, and countries buy from each other, so losses and falling demand pass along these links. It is not that all countries share the same banks. The spread comes from the connections.
a.clue: Think about how banks and countries are connected.

b.q: A large bank in Country A fails. Country B has a mining firm that sells most of its goods to Country A. What is the likely effect on Country B?
opts: Falling demand from Country A cuts the firm's sales
Nothing, because the bank failed in another country
Country B's firm sells more goods to Country A
Country B's banks are the only ones to be affected
b.why: Country A's trouble lowers its spending, so it buys fewer goods from Country B. This spreads the crisis through trade. Distance does not protect Country B, because the two economies are linked.
b.clue: Who buys the firm's goods, and what happens to their spending?

a.best: Banks and economies are linked by lending and trade

b.best: Falling demand from Country A cuts the firm's sales

problems.detail: The clue 'Think about how banks and countries are connected' points straight to the only option about connections. The other options (same banks everywhere, weather, copying laws) are implausible, so a student can pick the answer without knowing the idea.

proposal.remember: Links between banks and economies let a crisis in one country spread to others.

a.q: Banks based in Country A lose a lot of money at home. How might this hurt firms in Country B?
opts: The banks cut their lending to firms in Country B
The banks lend more in Country B to win back losses
Firms in Country B get cheaper loans from those banks
Firms in Country B are safe, as the losses stay in Country A
a.why: Banks that lose money in one place cut their lending in others, so firms in Country B find it harder to borrow. It is tempting to think the banks would lend more to make up their losses, but losing money leaves them less to lend.
a.clue: After a big loss, does a bank have more or less to lend?
